howDoI.q: How do I make a level that never scrolls?
How do I make a room that fills the screen exactly?
How do I choose which part of the map the screen starts on?
How do I make a level that scrolls to follow my hero?
How do I make a level longer than the screen?
How do I stop a scrolling level showing what is past its end?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Scroll or Stay is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has two short levels and takes a few minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the levels is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. F2 shows your lives, hit points and score. Walk into the door at the end of a level to go on.

Watch the picture rather than Kit: in the first level it never moves, and in the second it follows him. Nothing in this game can hurt you.

pages.head: Level 1: One Screen
pages.html:
Level 1: One Screen

THIS ROOM IS ONE SCREEN, SO IT DOES NOT SCROLL is the first sign. Kit starts in the middle of the room, and however he walks the picture stays where it is. THE HEDGE KEEPS KIT ON THE SCREEN is the second: walk left or right until the hedge stops him, and nothing is hidden behind it. Take the three coins and walk into the door at the right.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • Scrolling is off. Each scene in sc.gam has four scrolling settings: up, down, left and right. Each is on or off, and all four are off for this level's scene. The picture can then never move.
  • The screen is 16 blocks by 10. Open one.map in the map editor: the room is exactly that size, and every block of it is on screen all the time.
  • Kit starts in the middle. The engine begins every scene with the block where Kit starts in the middle of the screen. With scrolling off, that stays the view for good, so the room is laid out around his entrance: eight blocks to its left, seven to its right, five above and four below.
  • Hedges you can see. The room is closed in by hedge blocks on the left, right and top, and ground below. They are solid and they look it, so Kit is never stopped by something he cannot see.
  • The signs and the exit. The signs are ordinary blocks with words in their pictures. A scene link joins the door at the right to the next level in sc.gam.

pages.head: Level 2: The View Follows
pages.html:
Level 2: The View Follows

THE VIEW FOLLOWS KIT WHEN HE WALKS comes first, then a long, flat path with coins. Walk right and the picture slides after Kit once he is past the middle. THIS LEVEL IS 60 BLOCKS WIDE. THE SCREEN SHOWS 16 says how much of it you are seeing at a time. SCROLLING IS A SWITCH ON EACH SCENE comes near the end, and the door is beyond it.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • Scrolling is on. All four scrolling settings are on for this level's scene in sc.gam. The view starts to move once Kit is a few blocks from the middle of the screen and runs a little faster than he walks, then stops when he is a little past the middle the other way.
  • The level is 60 blocks wide. Open two.map in the map editor and scroll along it. A level can be any size up to the map's 100 by 100 blocks.
  • Every map is 100 by 100 blocks, and it wraps. The engine scrolls past the edge of a level and shows what is on the far side of the map, so this level's ends are closed with hedges and the ground and sky are carried on past them. Look at the left of two.map.
  • The signs and the exit. The signs are ordinary blocks with words in their pictures. The last door links to the The End scene in sc.gam.

pages.head: What it cannot do
pages.html:
What it cannot do

These are the engine's limits, so you can plan around them.

  • It cannot choose where the camera looks. The view follows the hero, starting with him in the middle. There is no setting to look ahead of him, hold on a place or pan to a spot.
  • It cannot change the screen's size. The screen is 16 blocks by 10, and a level that stays has to be exactly that.
  • It cannot switch scrolling on and off inside a level. It is a setting of the scene. To change it, send Kit through a door into another scene with the same map.
  • It cannot stop at the edge of the map. The map is 100 by 100 blocks and wraps, so a view that scrolls too far shows the far side. A level has to hide that with hedges and ground that carry on, as here.
  • It cannot zoom. Blocks are always drawn at one size.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • Turn level 1's scrolling on in its scene's settings, and watch the picture follow Kit past the room's edges.
  • Turn level 2's scrolling off, and see how little of the level you get.
  • Move level 1's entrance a few blocks and see where the screen sits.
  • Add a few blocks to level 1's room and walk to them.
  • Turn off only the up and down settings of a level, so the picture moves sideways and never up.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.
